summary: A local news feature listing ten ways residents can contribute to the cultural enrichment and preservation of historic neighborhoods, from joining heritage societies and giving tours to planting heritage gardens and hosting festivals. Each suggestion is illustrated by a named local resident or business owner. It frames these efforts as keeping neighborhood heritage vibrantly alive, building on the Old Town Heritage Committee's revitalization blueprint from September 2023.
one_line: Ten ways residents can help preserve and enrich historic neighborhoods, illustrated with examples from local residents and businesses.
key_facts: The Old Town Heritage Committee established its blueprint for revitalization in September 2023.
Jane Thompson, a long-time resident of Franklin Historic District, stewards a local heritage society.
Michael Johnson, a history teacher and local tour guide, stresses storytelling to bring history alive on neighborhood tours.
On October 15, 2023, Sarah Rodriguez led a successful campaign to pass a local ordinance giving tax incentives to homeowners who restored historic properties.
Tom Lee has organized over a dozen restoration projects since Thanksgiving 2023.
Emma Clarkson, owner of the Heritage Craft Market, says buying locally made products sustains the neighborhood's economic and cultural fabric.
David Kim, an amateur historian in Crescent Hill, started a digital archive of neighborhood history in early 2024.
Master gardener Linda Barnes says heritage gardens offer education about indigenous plants and historical planting techniques.
Jeffrey Peterson established a 1920s diner in 2023 as an example of a business reflecting historical character.
Lisa Nguyen is founder of the Old Town Culture Fest, which brings the community together and highlights the neighborhood's historical importance.
Marcus Davis hosts storytelling nights at the local library to preserve living history.
Restoration volunteering can include painting, gardening, carpentry, or stonework.
